summary: Tried to reproduce the user's bug: Dashboard shows Total Sales, but Reports > Sales Register is empty in a CA client business, in both the offline build (127.0.0.1:8765) and the online preview. With ONE window or tab, nothing failed. I added TEST_Client B through the UI, switched to it with the top switcher, saved 2 sales vouchers through New Voucher > Sales, and created an ERP client, project and invoice and finalized it. Dashboard Total Sales was Rs 8,500. The Sales Register (default dates, Combined) and the Total Sales KPI link both listed 3 rows with taxable Rs 8,500. Day Book, P&L, Trial Balance (balanced), Balance Sheet (balanced), GSTR-1, Project-wise P&L and Purchase Register (empty, no purchases) all matched the dashboard. Still fine after: reload on the register page, a second reload, switching to the home firm and back, and switching while Reports was open (the app goes back to the dashboard). The FY selector has only one year (2026-27), so the FY variation could not be tried. The bug DID reproduce, offline and online, as soon as TWO windows or tabs share the same storage. The business token is kept in localStorage ('eb_token', 'eb_biz'), which every window and tab shares. The business shown in the header and the selected FY are kept separately per window. So when window 2 switches business (or a new offline window starts up), window 1 keeps showing the client's name while all its requests go to the other business. Offline evidence: W1 dashboard request carried bid=TEST_Client B and showed Rs 8,500. W2 switched to My Business. W1 then clicked the Total Sales KPI: header still 'TEST_Client B', but the /api/reports/register request carried the home token (no bid claim) and returned the home firm's 1 row. Online evidence: fresh signup TEST_CA Firm, added TEST_Online Client, opened it, saved a sales voucher of Rs 700. Dashboard showed Rs 700 and the register 1 row. Tab 2 picked 'TEST_CA Firm (my firm)'. Tab 1, still headed 'TEST_Online Client', then showed 'No data for this period.' in the Sales Register, because the request went with the home token. That matches the user's report exactly. On the desktop app a second window is easy to open by accident: main.js setWindowOpenHandler allows any app URL, so Ctrl-, Shift- or middle-click on a sidebar item or KPI card opens a new window. That window's offline start() first writes the HOME token to localStorage and only then calls /ca/switch.

minor.issue: Reports.jsx always calls it; when the business has no ERP plan (online trial) it returns 402 and logs a console error on every Reports visit. The error is caught, but it is noise.

integration_issues.flow: CA business switch with two windows or tabs (offline desktop and online)
integration_issues.issue: The business token lives in localStorage, which all windows and tabs share. The business name, settings and FY shown are kept separately per window. Switching in one window silently moves every other window's requests to the new business while their headers still show the old one. Result: the Sales Register and every other report show another business's data (often empty), which is the user's bug. Writes are also at risk. A sales voucher saved from the stale tab was rejected with a misleading 'Select a valid party ledger' (its ledger IDs belong to the other business). Writes that carry no business-scoped IDs could land in the wrong business. Those are: new ledgers or parties, Settings save, stock items, CA add-client, ERP parties and projects, depreciation and tax posting. I did not test these to avoid changing data.

On every window load it first saves the HOME token (localStorage eb_token = /offline/session token) and only then calls /ca/switch. During that gap, other open windows send their requests to the home firm. If /ca/switch fails, it quietly removes eb_biz and every window falls back to the home firm.

action_items: HIGH: Keep the active business per window or tab. Store the switched token in sessionStorage (keep localStorage only as the default for new windows). Or send the business id as a header with every request (for example X-Business-Id, checked in get_current_user against memberships), taken from that window's own React state rather than shared storage.

HIGH (safety net): In AppContext, listen for window 'storage' events. When eb_token or eb_biz changes in another window, reload or re-sync user, settings and FY (or show a 'Business changed in another window' banner). That way a window can never show business A while sending requests for business B.
In the offline start(): do not write the home token before switching. Call /ca/switch with the session token passed as an explicit Authorization header, then write the final token once.
Optional: in main.js setWindowOpenHandler, deny same-origin app URLs (or open them in the same window) so Ctrl/Shift/middle-click on a Link cannot create a second app window.
Optional: show the business name taken from the API response on reports. Today the subtitle uses settings.company_name from the window's own state, so it hides the mismatch.
Minor: skip the /erp/projects call in Reports when ERP is not enabled, to avoid repeated 402 errors.
critical_code_review_comments: api.js reads localStorage eb_token on every request, so the token is shared by every window and tab, while useApp().user, settings and fy are per window. This split is the root cause.
BusinessSwitcher shows user.business_id from React state, not the business the token actually points at, so nothing on screen reveals the mismatch.
routes_reports.register and dashboard are correct: both are filtered by user.business_id from the token. For a single window, the API matched the dashboard for every client (new pytest file).

Dashboard total_sales is the movement on Sales-group ledgers across all voucher types, while the register lists only voucher_type=sales. They can legitimately differ if sales are posted by journal or receipt vouchers, or if credit notes exist. Consider a note or a link to the P&L.

success_rate.frontend: Single window: all flows pass. Multiple windows/tabs: FAIL (bug reproduced offline and online)

seed_data_creation: Offline repro DB (eb_offline_repro): client business 'TEST_Client B' (id 5d88a27d-bb67-46b4-ac96-9d2352c8717a) with 2 cash sales vouchers (Rs 1,000 and Rs 2,500 + GST), ERP party TEST_ERP Client, project PRJ-0001 'TEST Proj' and invoice INV/2026-27/0001, finalized as SAL/2026-27/0003. Neither was removed: there is no delete endpoint for businesses or vouchers. No pre-existing data was changed. The stale-tab voucher attempt was rejected with 400, so nothing was written to the wrong business.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To reproduce: one browser context, page1 switches to a client and opens the dashboard; page2 (same context) opens the app and switches to the home firm; page1 clicks kpi-total-sales. page1's header still shows the client, but the register request carries the home token. Decode the JWT payload: the 'bid' claim is missing for the home firm. After the fix, verify that each window keeps its own business, that reload keeps the business, and that offline start with two windows works. The offline server on 8765 was not restarted.
rca of the issue: Root cause: the selected business is stored per browser profile (localStorage eb_token and eb_biz), but each window keeps its own view state. Reproduction: (1) open the app, switch to a client, Dashboard shows the client's Total Sales. (2) Open a second window or tab of the app (offline: Ctrl, Shift or middle-click any link; online: a new tab) and pick the home firm there, or open any second offline window, whose start writes the home token. (3) Back in window 1, which still shows the client name, open Reports > Sales Register. The request /api/reports/register?voucher_type=sales&from_date=2026-04-01&to_date=2027-03-31 goes out with 'Authorization: Bearer <home-firm token>' (no bid claim) and returns the home firm's rows, often none, so the screen says 'No data for this period.' No console errors appear. The dashboard was right because it loaded before the token changed. Fix: keep the token or business per window (sessionStorage or an X-Business-Id header) and re-sync on storage events.
